problem:
A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(-2i+j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(6i-8j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(-8i-j)\,\text{km/h}.$

$t=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{h}$
worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=6i-8j,\,v=-8i-j,\,a=-2i+j,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ -8i-j & =(6i-8j)+(-2i+j)t \\ -14i+7j & =(-2i+j)t \\ -14i+7j & =-2ti+tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-14=-2t \\ 7=t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=7\,\text{h}.
$$
